::: {.eyebrow}
Open bioacoustic software
:::

This section will catalogue software and reproducible workflows developed for acoustic, behavioural, and vocal-sequence data. A tool will be listed only when its scope, dependencies, example data, validation status, licence, and citation information are documented.

::: {.status-badge .status-badge--developing}
In progress · first releases coming soon
:::

## Documentation required for release

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Analytical scope

The biological or computational question addressed, the intended input and output, and conditions under which a different method is preferable.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Reproducible example

Installation instructions, versioned dependencies, inspectable input data, expected output, and a complete minimal workflow.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Validation and status

An experimental, stable, or archived designation; tests or validation evidence; known limitations; version information; and the date of the most recent substantive update.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Licence and citation

An explicit software licence, citation guidance, source repository, release archive where appropriate, and instructions for reporting reproducible problems.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Until an individual tool page displays a licence, treat that tool as not yet released for reuse. Public source code without a licence is not automatically open-source software.
:::

::: {.collaboration-cta}
::: {.collaboration-cta__content}
## Try the tools—or tell me what would help

The tools will be free to use under their stated licences. If something breaks, if you test a workflow on another species, or if you have an idea that would make a tool more useful, please email me. I am especially happy to work closely when a technical problem grows out of a real research question.
:::
